statement: For every integer n>=0, let B_n be the permutations pi of [n] avoiding classical patterns 312 and 321 whose third compositional power pi^3 avoids 2143; no condition is imposed on pi^2. Let C_n be the ordered compositions of n with at most one part outside {1,3}, with one empty object in each set at n=0. Writing epsilon_d=(2,3,...,d,1), with epsilon_1=(1), the direct-sum map F(d_1,...,d_m)=epsilon_{d_1} direct-sum ... direct-sum epsilon_{d_m} restricts to a size-preserving bijection C_n -> B_n. Its inverse repeatedly records the position d of the minimum, removes the forced prefix epsilon_d, and subtracts d from the suffix. For every finite list of positive parts, F(d)^3 avoids 2143 if and only if at most one part is outside {1,3}. Consequently b_n=|B_n|=|C_n| for all n>=0 and, as a formal power-series identity, sum_{n>=0} b_n z^n = 1/(1-z-z^3) + (z^2+z^4/(1-z))/(1-z-z^3)^2.
contribution: A complete self-contained proof candidate for the cube enumeration explicitly conjectured in Section 5 of Archer--Bourne, arXiv:2505.05218v3. The known cyclic-block encoding is attributed and its inverse is verified; the cube calculation and two-inversion direct-sum criterion give the exact restriction and generating function. No later equivalent resolution was identified in the documented bounded primary-source search on 2026-09-12. Fresh mathematical review remains pending.
